observations: Photo 0: Black dual-cube 'spider' style moving-head light, each cube has 4 round lens openings (8 total), mounted on a yoke and base. Base has a red label reading something like 'LED MINI MOVING ...' but text is largely illegible/cut off.
Photo 0 background: shows a speaker box and a carton reading 'QUANTITY... SHIPPING W... DIMENSION:36...' confirming a shop/warehouse setting.
Photo 1: Same fixture powered on, emitting pink/purple/red beams from the lens openings, confirming at least some LEDs illuminate.
Photo 2: Fixture emitting a dense pattern of green laser lines onto the floor, indicating a separate laser module is built in, not mentioned clearly in the visible seller text.
No nameplate, model number, or brand logo is legible in any photo.
No video or photo shows the pan/tilt motor actually moving.

identity.kind: dual-head LED moving head stage light with built-in laser effect

claims.evidence: No nameplate or power rating sticker is readable in any photo.
No label or meter reading visible.
Photo 0 and Photo 1 show only 8 lens openings total (4 per cube x2), not 18 individual LEDs as claimed.
Photo 1 shows beams emitting from the lenses; Photo 2 shows an active laser pattern on the floor.
No photo or clip shows the head rotating or moving; static beam shots only.

risks.risk: Actual LED count/wattage may be lower than advertised, affecting brightness and price tier.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the nameplate/specification sticker on the base.
risks.if_unproven: priced as base-spec small LED moving head, not as high-wattage 18x10W unit

risks.risk: Pan/tilt motor or gearbox could be faulty or noisy, common failure point in used moving heads.
risks.proof: Short video clip showing the head panning and tilting through full range via DMX or master/slave mode.
risks.if_unproven: priced as static/non-moving unit (motor function not confirmed)

risks.risk: DMX/control board functionality (sound-active, DMX channels) not demonstrated.
risks.proof: Clip showing DMX controller or sound-activation responding to the fixture.
risks.if_unproven: priced as basic auto-mode only, no DMX control assumed

risks.risk: Physical condition (dents, cracked lenses, loose yoke) may be hidden by camera angle/lighting.
risks.proof: Clear daylight photos from multiple angles including underside and lens close-ups.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming cosmetic wear consistent with used stage equipment

risks.risk: Laser module safety/class and functionality beyond the single demo shot unverifiable.
risks.proof: Longer video showing laser operating continuously without flicker or dropout.
risks.if_unproven: priced as laser present but unverified reliability

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the nameplate/spec sticker on the base showing actual wattage, voltage, and LED count.
Video clip of the head panning/tilting and switching through color/strobe modes.
Photo of the unit from additional angles (rear, underside) showing physical condition.
Confirmation of DMX or sound-active control functioning.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable by type as a dual-head LED moving light with laser effect, and photos show it powered and emitting light/laser, but the specific wattage/LED-count claim is contradicted by the visible lens count and motor/DMX function is unverified, so it should be priced at the worst-case (basic working light, unverified motor/control) until further proof is given.
